purpose: Candidate retrieval, scoped feature lookup, and concept-graph membership. LLM review decides identity and applicability.

object.definition: There are $K\ge2$ arms. The reward laws $\nu_{t,i}$ are fixed before interaction, supported on $[0,1]$, and sampled independently across rounds. Denote means by $\mu_{t,i}=\mathbb E X_{t,i}$ and their vector by $\mu_t$. $$V_\mu=\sum_{t=2}^{T}\|\mu_t-\mu_{t-1}\|_\infty,\qquad Q_{\mathrm{env}}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\max_{1\le i\le K}\operatorname{Var}(X_{t,i})\le\frac T4.$$ The quantity $Q_{\mathrm{env}}$ sums the largest arm variance in each round; it is neither the variance sum along the chosen arms nor the sum over all arms.

feedback_quality.noise: heteroscedastic, possibly zero variance; laws need not be stationary even if means constant

operation.query_signature: Choose arm $I_t$ and receive one reward $X_{t,I_t}$. Noise may be heteroscedastic or zero; reward laws may vary over time even with constant means. Inputs $K,T$ and mean-drift bound $V$ satisfying $V_\mu\le V$ are public. Armwise variances, means, change locations, and variance budget $Q$ are hidden. A causal policy cannot use undisclosed budgets and must work simultaneously across all such unknown-budget classes. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally. No unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available; any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.

protocols.adversary_information: Follow the model and oracle timing. Current private random realizations are not visible to the environment.
protocols.loss_bearing_points: The output is the complete action trajectory satisfying feasibility and timing requirements. Randomized mixtures may be implemented before acting. Retrospective averages or convex combinations cannot replace actions that have already incurred loss. No additional optimal value or certificate is required.
protocols.past_requery: History may be stored. New information from old samples or past rounds is unavailable unless the native interface explicitly permits it.
steps: The algorithm chooses arm $I_t$ before receiving one reward $X_{t,I_t}$. Noise may be heteroscedastic or zero. Reward distributions may change across rounds even when their means remain constant.
Public inputs are $K,T$ and mean-drift bound $V$, with $V_\mu\le V$.
Per-arm per-round variances, means, and change locations are hidden; variance budget $Q$ is also hidden.
The algorithm must be causal and cannot depend on unavailable budgets. One policy must work simultaneously across all such unknown-budget classes.

Received feedback may be stored and reused in computation. Unrevealed information cannot be requested from past rounds, and consumed random samples cannot receive additional queries. Current-round exceptions are limited to the explicitly supplied full-function access or same-sample two-point interface.

variable_blocks.space: $I_t\in[K]$; exactly one arm is selected at a time.
